Tap to show controls

From any screen to after dark.

Mac or Windows · no installation

  1. Download the desktop app. Save Hauntlight.html to a folder or your Desktop. Double-click it to open in a modern browser. If it opens in a text editor, use Open With and choose your browser. No account, Python, Node, or internet connection is needed to use the downloaded app.
  2. Connect your projector. Use HDMI or your computer’s screen-mirroring setup. With an extended desktop, move this browser window onto the projector before aligning. The editor and projection use the same window; a separate remote control window is not provided.
  3. Align, then project. Choose a scene, use Align and the corner controls, then Project. If fullscreen is unavailable, maximize the window. Tap or click to reveal controls; Escape returns to the editor, and B toggles blackout in projection mode.

iPad

Open the hosted version in Safari. Use Share → Add to Home Screen for a shortcut. Mirror through Apple TV or a suitable HDMI adapter. On iPad 5, start with Auto quality and 1–3 surfaces. For an Epson 980W, use an Apple TV connected to HDMI for AirPlay; the projector is not a native AirPlay receiver.

Keep your layout

Use Export layout to save a JSON backup and Import layout to restore it. Automatic saving depends on the browser. Local-file storage can change when you rename, move, or replace the app. An app download contains the default scenes, not your personal layout.

A few projection tips

Keep the screen awake and the device on power. Use the same window size, screen orientation and fullscreen state for alignment and projection. The canvas is 16:10; preserve its aspect ratio on the projector. Black pixels cannot remove the projector’s residual light. Use after dark on matte surfaces, and keep indoor projectors dry.

Choose Any orientation for 10 scenes without a preferred up/down direction. All 24 scenes are procedural and included in the desktop download.

Hauntlight is MIT-licensed and includes the MIT-licensed perspective-transform core. Hardware performance and mirroring depend on your setup.
